fields.description:
## Context
S1 provides one budgeted atomic summary executor and S2 provides immutable plans, but compound legacy dispatch can replay successful early work and conflates applied, deferred, and failed outcomes.

## Outcome
Add a provider-neutral coordinator and failure policy for update, delete, probe, clean-label, repair-property, and conflict plans. Execute atomic desired postconditions in dependency order and re-observe only remaining drift after partial success.

## Plan
1. Define normalized success, recovered, deferred, permanent, `commit_unknown`, exhausted-transient, and skipped dispositions with ticket/endpoint/tenant/provider/global scope.
2. Consume immutable plans, enforce their dependencies, and call adapter atomic operations through the S1 budget.
3. Preserve proven earlier postconditions after a late failure; re-observe and plan only remaining drift instead of replaying the compound mutation.
4. Treat already-gone delete as idempotent success, ticket-local 404/permanent 4xx as ticket-scoped, and authoritative broad failures only at their declared scope.
5. Produce exact per-ticket applied/failed/deferred/skipped/recovered outcomes without implementing a fuse yet.

## Testing
Coordinator tables cover dependencies, partial update, delete, ticket-local 404, permanent 4xx, auth/quota/rate scopes, and independent continuation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Non-create plans execute atomic postconditions once in dependency order.
- [ ] Late failure preserves proven earlier success and re-observes only remaining drift.
- [ ] Already-gone delete is idempotent success.
- [ ] Ticket-local and permanent failures isolate the ticket, while authoritative broad failures stop only their declared scope.
- [ ] Independent tickets and endpoints continue.
- [ ] Per-ticket outcome fields and tallies distinguish applied, failed, deferred, skipped, and recovered work exactly.

## Out of scope
Finite-pass fuse thresholds and production family cutover remain later S3 tasks.
## Impacted sites (existing consumer/construction seams this change touches)
- `typed_dispatch.py:44` `_build_leaves()` — the `(direction, action) -> leaf callable` table for outbound update/delete/probe and inbound update; the new coordinator becomes authoritative for these non-create leaves. New routing is additive/shadow; existing leaves stay callable.
- `retry_budget.py` — S1 budget the coordinator calls atomic adapter ops through: `RetryBudget.attempt_retry` (:112), `decide_replay` (:132), `replay_safety_for` (:144). No signature change; consumed as-is.
- `dispatch_one.py` (existing, 740 LOC) — existing single-op atomic executors reused for postconditions: `update_one` (:423), scalar/label/parent helpers (:599/:714/:514). **800-LOC cap risk**: net-new coordinator logic lands in the new `coordinator.py`/`failure_policy.py`, NOT by growing `dispatch_one.py` past cap.
- `operation_outcome.py` `Disposition` — normalized disposition vocabulary (applied, already_satisfied, recovered, retryable_deferred, commit_unknown, permanent_failure, exhausted_transient, dependency_deferred, scope_deferred, safety_aborted, skipped); failure_policy maps outcomes onto these.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_applier_stale_binding_404.py` (existing, 282 LOC) — ticket-local 404 isolation regression, extended for the coordinator's idempotent-delete/404-isolation behavior.

Fuse thresholds (S3 T2) and production family cutover (S3 T3) are explicitly out of scope; new routing stays shadow/additive with legacy dispatch authoritative.
